scope: Additive Materials Lab v1 review-candidate questions; frozen and historical questions remain unchanged. Implementation is distinct from production activation and platform acceptance.

questions.query: How do I open Materials Lab v1 and inspect declared versus effective native material physics?
facts: The review candidate mounts in the desktop feature launcher and Shared Workbench, or --materials-lab.
The matching native bridge is required; native facts are not replaced by shadow or fallback metadata.
Rows distinguish declared/effective values, actual consumer, applicability and editability; Workbench policy is a copied receipt at opening.

questions.query: Which Materials Lab candidate properties are editable, and does compiled/tested mean runtime-active?
facts: Density, RGBA, explicit capabilities and visual projection are editable isolated candidates; viscosity is limited to supported yielding templates.
Kernel, physical state, movement and state defaults remain held to the selected template.
Draft, validated, compiled/tested and runtime-active are distinct; existing-ID candidates execute in an external compiled World, with no production installer.

questions.query: How do material presets round-trip and compile the synthetic non-hard powder at ID132?
facts: Version1 envelopes contain a strict candidate, source catalogue hash and deterministic digest; malformed or tampered imports preserve the current candidate.
The synthetic132 fixture compiles density1337, RGBA17/91/203/255, hardfalse and granulartrue without production ID allocation.
Compiled bundles use an external fresh directory and source/generated/executable hashes; the frozen compatibility lock is unchanged.

questions.query: What does a threshold0 candidate reaction mean, and are keep_existing or state-setting effects supported?
facts: Threshold T means inclusive (T+1)/256;0 succeeds for roll0 and fails for roll1.

Effects v1 retain replacement defaults; isolated World effects v2 admit non-Water keep_existing and declared Metal/Combustible state_b updates. Unsupported state/quantity contracts and conflicts are rejected.
The actual sparse native resolver is tested over256rolls and both orientations; World scheduling or sleep eligibility is not inferred.

questions.query: How do Materials Lab native simulation test cases reproduce Salt plus Water with source and worker identity?
facts: The existing MicroScenario host owns an isolated native World, with source, definition, seed, worker count and Water-family configuration retained.
The fixture observes768Brine after120ticks; native counts/state/quantities/hashes are authoritative, not images.
Fresh reference comparison and saved-case reconstruction are supported; one/four workers are tested and source mismatch refuses import.

questions.query: Can Materials Lab v1 install authored physics, and which production compatibility gates remain separate?
facts: Production132slots including invalid10,56rules, source identity and saved-world semantics remain unchanged.
Production activation remains a separately qualified353-B consumer/identity transition.
The owner excluded MoltenGlass H1 from this continuation; it is not a Materials Lab delivery dependency.

questions.query: How can I compare an edited material in a compiled native World against untouched source and inspect actual cells and quantities?
facts: Candidate test compiles the native World twice: untouched reference and externally adapted generated tables, with matching recipe and default solver configuration.
Density500 Sand and authored Salt/Water products have actual stored-cell outcomes; repeat, one/four workers, same-build persistence and quantity checks accompany the receipt.
Synthetic132 and changed hard/granular or visual-state capabilities are refused by this World backend. Production activation and cross-build saves remain unqualified.

questions.query: How do I save and import a source-bound candidate World recipe with the same material, partner, seed, ticks and workers?
facts: Save World recipe writes a strict versioned case containing the candidate, scenario and native-input source hashes with deterministic digests.
Import restores the candidate and visible controls as Validated candidate, clears prior test evidence and requires a fresh compiled World run.
Executable source changes, malformed fields and tampered digests refuse import; Git metadata-only changes do not invalidate identical inputs.

questions.query: How does native contact inspection distinguish masks and source-core window exclusion from a supplied reaction probability roll?
facts: Left and right preview clicks select source and target; inspection pauses the exclusive owner and copies actual stored/visible IDs, state, temperature and masks at one completed tick.
The report distinguishes neighbour, source-core and mask facts from the compiled resolver result at a supplied byte roll; target-core halo access is not incorrectly excluded.
Per-cell sleeping, future deadlines, epochs, task dispatch and actual random bytes remain unobserved; inspection never executes a reaction and step/input changes retire it.

questions.query: How do I open the Windows Materials Lab evaluation package without installing Python Git and a compiler, and what proves it was tested?
facts: Extract the complete evaluation ZIP to a writable directory and run Open-Materials-Lab.cmd; keep source and dependencies together.
The branch-scoped publisher requires actual Windows native authoring and graphical receipts, then executes the copied package environment before delivery.
The manifest binds the native DLL and all package files; automated platform execution does not claim human acceptance or runtime activation of authored physics.
